nodes.summary: Decoding a pair $(A, s)$ of a natural number $A$ and a list $s$ of elements of the disjoint union $\mathbb{N} \sqcup T$ gives the production, with terminals $T$ and nonterminals $\mathbb{N}$, whose left-hand side is the nonterminal $A$ and whose right-hand side is $s$ with each entry decoded as a symbol: a number $i$ from the left summand becomes the nonterminal $i$ and an element $a$ of $T$ becomes the terminal $a$.
nodes.title: Decoding a production

nodes.summary: Decoding sends an element of the disjoint union $\mathbb{N} \sqcup T$ to a grammar symbol with terminals $T$ and nonterminals $\mathbb{N}$: a natural number $i$ from the left summand goes to the nonterminal $i$, and an element $a$ of $T$ from the right summand goes to the terminal $a$.
nodes.title: Decoding a grammar symbol

nodes.summary: Encoding a production with terminals $T$ and nonterminals $\mathbb{N}$ gives the pair $(A, s)$ where $A \in \mathbb{N}$ is its left-hand side and $s$ is its right-hand side with each symbol encoded as an element of the disjoint union $\mathbb{N} \sqcup T$: the terminal $a$ becomes $a$ in the right summand and the nonterminal $i$ becomes $i$ in the left summand.
nodes.title: Encoding a production

nodes.summary: Encoding sends a grammar symbol with terminals $T$ and nonterminals $\mathbb{N}$ to an element of the disjoint union $\mathbb{N} \sqcup T$: the terminal $a$ goes to $a$ in the right summand $T$, and the nonterminal $i$ goes to $i$ in the left summand $\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Encoding a grammar symbol

nodes.summary: An encoded context-free grammar over a terminal type $T$ consists of a start nonterminal, which is a natural number, and a list of productions. Each production is a pair of a left-hand side, a natural number, and a right-hand side, a list of elements of the disjoint union $\mathbb{N} \sqcup T$, in which a number $i$ from the left summand stands for nonterminal $i$ and an element $a$ of $T$ for terminal $a$.
nodes.title: Encoded context-free grammars

nodes.summary: Sending an encoded grammar over $T$ to the pair of its start nonterminal and its list of productions is a bijection from encoded grammars over $T$ onto pairs $(s, R)$ of a natural number $s$ and a list $R$ of pairs of a natural number and a list of elements of the disjoint union $\mathbb{N} \sqcup T$.
nodes.title: Encoded grammars as pairs

nodes.summary: A language is context-free exactly when an encoded grammar generates it.
nodes.title: A language is context-free exactly when an encoded grammar generates it

nodes.summary: Let $g$ and $G$ be context-free grammars over the same terminals. Suppose there are maps $f$ from the nonterminals of $g$ to those of $G$ and $b$ from the nonterminals of $G$ to those of $g$ such that renaming the nonterminals of any production of $g$ by $f$ gives a production of $G$, renaming the nonterminals of any production of $G$ by $b$ gives a production of $g$, $f$ sends the start nonterminal of $g$ to that…
nodes.title: Grammars with renamings in both directions generate the same language

nodes.summary: The language of an encoded grammar is context-free.
nodes.title: Encoded grammars generate context-free languages

nodes.summary: The encoding of a grammar generates the same language.
nodes.title: The encoding of a grammar generates the same language

nodes.summary: The language of an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$ is the language generated by the context-free grammar that $g$ denotes, whose nonterminals are the natural numbers, whose initial nonterminal is the start nonterminal of $g$ and whose productions are the decoded productions of $g$.
nodes.title: Language of an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a context-free grammar over $T$ and $r$ a production of $G$. Replacing each nonterminal $A$ of $r$ by its number, the position, counting from $0$, of the first occurrence of $A$ in the list of nonterminals that $G$ mentions, and then replacing each number $n$ by the nonterminal of $G$ with number $n$ (the entry at position $n$ of that list, or the initial nonterminal of $G$ if the list has no such entry)…
nodes.title: Numbering the nonterminals of a production and back recovers it

nodes.summary: For maps $f : N_1 \to N_2$ and $b : N_2 \to N_3$ and a grammar symbol $s$ with terminals in $T$ and nonterminals in $N_1$, renaming the nonterminals of $s$ by $f$ and then by $b$ gives the same symbol as renaming them by $b \circ f$.
nodes.title: Renaming the nonterminals of a symbol twice

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $G$, the number of a nonterminal $A$ of $G$ is the position, counting from $0$, of the first occurrence of $A$ in the list of nonterminals that $G$ mentions (its initial nonterminal first); if $A$ does not occur in that list, its number is the length of the list.
nodes.title: Numbering of nonterminals

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $G$ and a natural number $n$, the nonterminal of $G$ with number $n$ is the entry at position $n$, counting from $0$, of the list of nonterminals that $G$ mentions (its initial nonterminal first); if the list has no entry at position $n$, it is the initial nonterminal of $G$.
nodes.title: Nonterminal with a given number

nodes.summary: The partial map from grammar symbols with terminals in $T$ and nonterminals in $N$ to $N$ that sends a nonterminal $A$ to $A$ and has no value on terminals.
nodes.title: Nonterminal of a symbol

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $G$ over $T$, the encoded grammar whose start nonterminal is the number of the initial nonterminal of $G$ and whose productions are the productions of $G$, listed in some fixed order, with every nonterminal $A$ replaced by its number, the position, counting from $0$, of the first occurrence of $A$ in the list of nonterminals that $G$ mentions (its initial nonterminal first).
nodes.title: Encoding of a context-free grammar

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$, the context-free grammar over $T$ whose nonterminals are the natural numbers, whose initial nonterminal is the start nonterminal of $g$, and whose productions are the decodings of the encoded productions of $g$: an encoded production $(i, u)$ becomes the production rewriting the nonterminal $i$ to the word obtained from $u$ by reading each entry $\mathrm{inl}\, j$…
nodes.title: Grammar denoted by an encoding

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $G$, the list consisting of the initial nonterminal of $G$ followed, for each production of $G$ in turn (in some fixed order of its finite set of productions), by the left-hand side of the production and then the nonterminals of its right-hand side in order. Nonterminals may occur more than once.
nodes.title: List of nonterminals mentioned by a grammar

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
